He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffaloes]] and earned first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]] as a sophomore in 2013. He missed most of his junior year after injuring his [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL). Dinwiddie recovered and was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the second round of the [[2014 NBA draft]]. After two seasons with the Pistons, he joined the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in December 2016 and played with them until being traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2021. In February 2022, Dinwiddie was traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] and in 2023, he was traded back to the Brooklyn Nets and was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] the following year in February 2024 before being immediately waived by Toronto. He signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the remainder of the season in a bench role. ==High school career== At [[William Howard Taft High School (Los Angeles)|William Howard Taft High School]], Dinwiddie was recognized as one of the greatest standout athletes since [[Jordan Farmar]]. He averaged 5.9 points and 4.1 assists as the starting [[point guard]] alongside a fellow [[2014 NBA draft|2014 draftee]] in [[DeAndre Daniels]] at the conclusion of his junior season. Dinwiddie maximized his game as he began his final year representing the school, averaging 11.2 points and 7.7 assists. He was one of the most skilled passers in school history, and became the John R. Wooden California High School Player of the Year in 2011. However, [[Long Beach Polytechnic High School|Long Beach Poly]]'s Ryan Anderson was named [[California Mr. Basketball]]. Dinwiddie became just one of seven players that won the prestigious award as a senior. The powerful duo of Daniels and Dinwiddie won the city championship this season as well. This final season at Taft helped Dinwiddie gain the attention of colleges around the country. He chose to attend [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] rather than [[Harvard Crimson men's basketball|Harvard]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]], or [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]]. Considered a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Dinwiddie was listed as the No. 25-point guard and the No. 146 player in the nation in 2011.{{cite web|title=Spencer Dinwiddie Recruiting Profile|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Spencer-Dinwiddie-113200|work=Rivals.com|access-date=June 30, 2014}} ==College career== ===Freshman season (2011–2012)=== In the first regular season game for [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]], Dinwiddie made his collegiate debut in a 32-point victory over [[Fort Lewis Skyhawks|Fort Lewis]] with seven points and seven rebounds. He shot just 2-for-9 from the [[Field goal (basketball)|field]].{{cite web|title=Colorado 85, Fort Lewis 57|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313150038|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306124209/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313150038|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 6, 2012|publisher=ESPN|date=November 11, 2011|access-date=June 30, 2014}} Dinwiddie reached double figures in his sixth appearance, which was against [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|Georgia]]. This was the first time he had shot over .500 on field goals up till then. The [[California]] native led the team to this win and made three key free throws in the final seconds.{{cite web|title=Colorado 70, Georgia 68|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313320038|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306134505/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313320038|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 6, 2012|publisher=ESPN|date=November 28, 2011|access-date=June 30, 2014}} Dinwiddie teamed with fellow freshman [[Askia Booker]], forming another duo on his new team. They combined for 677 points, making school history by scoring over 250 points each. At the conclusion of the season, they were the only Buffaloes to do so. Dinwiddie became a member of the Pac-12 Conference Tournament Championship Team. He led Colorado in free throw percentage and ranked third among freshmen in that category.{{cite web|title=Colorado Buffaloes 2011–12 Statistics|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/stats/_/id/38/year/2012/colorado-buffaloes|publisher=ESPN|access-date=June 27, 2014}} By the end of the regular season, Dinwiddie had helped the team earn its first [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA men's basketball tournament]] berth since the 2002–03 season.{{cite web|title=2002–03 Colorado Buffaloes Roster|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/colorado/2003.html|website=Sports-reference.com|access-date=June 30, 2014}} Shooting [[Three-point field goal|three -pointers]] at a .438 clip, Dinwiddie was named to the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] All-Freshman Team with [[Tony Wroten]].{{cite web|last1=Topham|first1=David|title=Detroit Pistons: Analyzing the Spencer Dinwiddie pick|url=http://isportsweb.com/2014/06/29/detroit-pistons-analyzing-spencer-dinwiddie-pick/|website=isportsweb.com|date=June 29, 2014|access-date=June 30, 2014}} He was the only Pac-12 freshman to have a field-goal percentage of over .400 total. ===Sophomore season (2012–2013)=== The departures of [[Carlon Brown]] and Nate Tomlinson were instrumental in Dinwiddie's breakout sophomore season, when he earned first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] honors.{{cite news|last=Yoon |first=Peter |title=Shabazz Muhammad, Larry Drew II named All-Pac-12 |date=March 11, 2013 |publisher=ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/13549/shabazz-muhammad-larry-drew-ii-named-all-pac-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130314032008/http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/13549/shabazz-muhammad-larry-drew-ii-named-all-pac-12 |archive-date=March 14, 2013 |url-status=live }} Leading the team in assists, they reached the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA men's basketball tournament]] for the second consecutive season, in which they reached the second round. It was the first time the team had reached back-to-back tournaments since the 1963 season. The Buffaloes won the 2012 [[Charleston Classic]], in which Dinwiddie took the role as starting [[small forward]] in the final three rounds. He was just one of two players – the other being Askia Booker – to start all 33 games. By the end of the season, Booker and Dinwiddie became the highest sophomore scoring tandem in school history. Dinwiddie led the team in assists 20 times and was the top scorer on 15 different occasions. He recorded 29 points in a home win over [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]], which marked his own career-high scoring record. On February 10, 2012, Dinwiddie recorded a perfect game against [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]]. He shot 6-for-6 from the field, 4-for-4 from beyond the arc, and 8-for-8 on free throws. This set the school record for most points scored without missing a single shot.{{cite web|title=Spencer Dinwiddie Player Profile|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Spencer-Dinwiddie/GameLogs/30385/NCAA/2013/All|website=RealGM.com|access-date=June 30, 2014}} He made the remark, "I see over people and I shoot over people... for the smaller point guards, they don't really get to contest me." The [[William Howard Taft Charter High School (Los Angeles)|Taft]] graduate stood {{height|ft=6|in=6}} by the end of the season.{{cite web|last1=Thorburn|first1=Ryan|title=Men's basketball: CU Buffs will rely on Askia Booker and Spencer Dinwiddie|url=http://www.dailycamera.com/ci_21804927/mens-basketball-cu-buffs-will-rely-askia-booker|work=Daily Camera|date=October 18, 2012|access-date=June 27, 2014}} ===Junior season (2013–2014)=== Dinwiddie continued to act as the leader of the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball]] team through the beginning of his junior year. He helped the team win 14 of their first 16 regular season games, which made them one of the most successful underdogs in the country, most notably toppling the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] due to a game-winner from [[Askia Booker]].{{cite web|last=Dauster|first=Rob|title=Colorado needs game-winner to serve as a catalyst for Askia Booker (Video)|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/12/07/askia-booker-beats-kansas-at-the-buzzer-video/|website=NBCSports.com|date=December 7, 2013|access-date=June 27, 2014}} Dinwiddie was considered the catalyst for the unanticipated run from his team, however. On November 21, 2012, he shot a career-best 14-for-15 from the [[Free throw|free throw line]] against [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|Santa Barbara]]. Colorado won each game in which their top scorer scored 20 or more points total. On January 12, 2014, Dinwiddie suffered a career-threatening [[ACL injury]] against [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]], forcing him to sit out for the remainder of the season. As his junior season was cut short, the team finished the year just 23–12; their record was 14–2 while Dinwiddie was healthy. Dinwiddie reportedly made contact with Russ Paine, who helped [[Adrian Peterson]] recover from his ACL injury and become the 2012 [[National Football League Most Valuable Player Award|NFL MVP]].{{cite web|last1=Goodman|first1=Jeff|title=Spencer Dinwiddie has torn ACL|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10288706/colorado-buffaloes-star-spencer-dinwiddie-season|publisher=ESPN|date=January 15, 2014|access-date=June 27, 2014}}{{cite web|last1=Savage|first1=Brendan|title=Get to know, Spencer Dinwiddie: Detroit Pistons draft pick rehabbed with NFL star's therapist|url=http://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2014/06/get_to_know_spencer_dinwiddie.html|website=MLive|date=June 27, 2014|access-date=June 30, 2014}} On April 24, 2014, Dinwiddie declared for the NBA draft, foregoing his final year of college eligibility.{{cite web|last1=Kensler|first1=Tom|title=CU Buffs point guard Spencer Dinwiddie declares for the 2014 NBA draft|url=http://www.denverpost.com/colleges/ci_25630281/cus-spencer-dinwiddie-will-forego-senior-year-declares|work=The Denver Post|date=April 24, 2014|access-date=April 24, 2014}} ==Professional career== ===Detroit Pistons (2014–2016)=== [[File:Spencer Dinwiddie, Ramon Sessions (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|left|Dinwiddie with the Pistons in February 2015]] Dinwiddie was selected with the 38th overall pick by the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the [[2014 NBA draft]].{{cite web|last1=Valdez|first1=Alexandria|title=Spencer Dinwiddie drafted by Pistons in second round at No. 38|url=http://www.denverpost.com/nuggets/ci_26043122/spencer-dinwiddie-drafted-by-pistons-second-round-at|work=The Denver Post|date=June 26, 2014|access-date=June 27, 2014}} He appeared in 34 games for the Pistons as a rookie, making one start{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/dinwisp01/gamelog/2015/|title=Spencer Dinwiddie 2014–15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 2, 2019}} and receiving two assignments to the [[Grand Rapids Drive]], the Pistons' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=March 2, 2019}} His lone start came on February 20, 2015, after a pair of trades left the Pistons short-handed. He had career highs of 12 points and nine assists in a 100–91 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150220/CHIDET/gameinfo.html|title=Drummond, Dinwiddie lead thin Pistons past Bulls 100–91|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 20, 2015|access-date=February 20, 2015}} Eight days later, he scored a season-best 20 points to go with eight assists in 25 minutes off the [[bench (sport)|bench]] in a 99–95 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150228/DETWAS/gameinfo.html|title=Wizards end losing streak with 99–95 win over Pistons|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 28, 2015|access-date=February 28, 2015}} The 2015–16 season saw Dinwiddie appear in just 12 regular-season games for the Pistons, after spending the majority of the season in the D-League with the Grand Rapids Drive. After back-up [[Steve Blake]] opened the season in a shooting slump,{{cite web|last=Hinson|first=Steve|url=https://www.detroitbadboys.com/2016/5/10/11605952/2015-16-pistons-review-spencer-dinwiddie-running-out-of-chances|title=2015–16 Pistons Review: Spencer Dinwiddie running out of chances|work=detroitbadboys.com|date=May 10, 2016|access-date=March 2, 2019}} Dinwiddie received his first opportunity of the season in the tenth game, scoring 17 points on November 15 in a 97–85 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400828038|title=Kobe Bryant, Jordan Clarkson lead Lakers past Pistons|publisher=ESPN|date=November 15, 2015|access-date=March 2, 2019}} However, after struggling in the next four games, he fell out of the rotation, compounded by Blake's form improvement and [[Brandon Jennings]] returning from injury. Dinwiddie played a season-high 29 minutes in the Pistons' regular-season finale on April 13, scoring 12 points in a 112–110 overtime win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/dinwisp01/gamelog/2016/|title=Spencer Dinwiddie 2015–16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 2, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400829107|title=Pistons vs. Cavaliers – Box Score|publisher=ESPN|date=April 13, 2016|access-date=March 2, 2019}} He then appeared in game two of the Pistons' 4–0 first-round playoff series loss to the Cavaliers. ===Windy City Bulls (2016)=== On June 17, 2016, Dinwiddie was traded to the Chicago Bulls in exchange for [[Cameron Bairstow]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/release/bulls-acquire-spencer-dinwiddie-cameron-bairstow|title=Bulls Acquire Spencer Dinwiddie For Cameron Bairstow|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=June 17, 2016|access-date=June 17, 2016}} He was waived by the Bulls on July 7,{{cite web|url=http://www.csnchicago.com/chicago-bulls/report-bulls-waive-point-guard-spencer-dinwiddie|title=Report: Bulls Waive Point Guard Spencer Dinwiddie|work=csnchicago.com|date=July 7, 2016|access-date=July 28, 2016}} re-signed on July 28,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-spencer-dinwiddie-728|title=Bulls Sign Spencer Dinwiddie|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 28, 2016|access-date=July 28, 2016}} and waived again on October 21 after appearing in five preseason games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/release/bulls-waive-spencer-dinwiddie|title=Bulls Waive Spencer Dinwiddie|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 21, 2016|access-date=October 21, 2016}} He then spent the start of the 2016–17 season with Chicago's D-League affiliate team, the [[Windy City Bulls]],{{cite web|url=http://windycity.dleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-bulls-select-four-players-2016-d-league-draft-complete-training-camp-roster/|title=Windy City Bulls Select Four Players in 2016 D-League Draft to Complete Training Camp Roster|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 30, 2016|access-date=December 5, 2016}} averaging 19.4 points, 8.1 assists and 3.7 rebounds over 37.4 minutes in nine games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2016/12/08/brooklyn-nets-spencer-dinwiddie|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Spencer Dinwiddie|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=December 8, 2016|access-date=December 8, 2016}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2016–2021)=== On December 8, 2016, Dinwiddie signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. On February 15, 2017, he scored 15 of his season-high 19 points in the fourth quarter of the Nets' 129–125 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900244|title=Antetokounmpo scores 33, Bucks hold off Nets 129–125|publisher=ESPN|date=February 15, 2017|access-date=March 2, 2019}} On April 8, 2017, in a 107–106 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]], Dinwiddie made four free throws in the final 13.6 seconds and finished with 19 points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900566|title=Wade returns but Nets hand Bulls potentially costly loss|publisher=ESPN|date=April 8, 2017|access-date=March 2, 2019}} [[File:Dinwiddie Nets 2018.jpg|thumb|right|Dinwiddie in 2018]] On October 25, 2017, Dinwiddie scored a career-high 22 points and hit the go-ahead 3-pointer with 43 seconds left to lift the Nets to a 112–107 win over set a new career high with 25 points in a 118–107 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974970|title=Dinwiddie scores 25, leads Nets over Jazz, he tied his career high with 26 points in a 123–119 overtime loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975233|title=Oladipo scores 38, Pacers rally to beat against the Cavaliers on March 6, Dinwiddie had his 14th 20-point game off the bench to set a Nets single-season record—[[Darryl Dawkins]], [[Purvis Short]] and [[Orlando Woolridge]] all had 13.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071642|title=Dinwiddie leads Nets in 4th as they beat Cavs 113–107|publisher=ESPN|date=March 6, 2019|access-date=March 7, 2019}} With 23 points against the Hawks on March 9, Dinwiddie surpassed [[Armen Gilliam]] in 1993–94 with the most single-season points in a reserve role.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071660|title=Nets hold off Hawks 114–112 for 3rd straight win|publisher=ESPN|date=March 9, 2019|access-date=March 9, 2019}} During the [[2019–20 NBA season]], Dinwiddie began the season as a reserve until [[Kyrie Irving]] injured his shoulder.{{cite news|last=Andrews|first=Malika|title=Source: Nets' Spencer Dinwiddie trying to join Nigerian national team|date=April 18, 2020|publisher=ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29060857/andrew-bogut-says-retirement-decision-come-mid-may|access-date=April 19, 2020}} On January 28, 2020, Dinwiddie switched his jersey number from 8 to 26 after the approval of the NBA, in honor of the late [[Kobe Bryant]].{{cite web |title=Spencer Dinwiddie, Terrence Ross change jersey numbers after Kobe Bryant's passing |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/01/28/spencer-dinwiddie-terrence-ross-jersey-number-change |publisher=National Basketball Association |access-date=January 28, 2020 |date=January 28, 2020}} On June 29, 2020, Dinwiddie announced that he had tested positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]].{{cite web |last1=Wojnarowski |first1=Adrian |title=Nets' DeAndre Jordan, Spencer Dinwiddie say they tested positive for the coronavirus |date=June 29, 2020 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29385011/nets-deandre-jordan-spencer-dinwiddie-say-tested-positive-coronavirus |publisher=ESPN |access-date=June 30, 2020}} On December 27, 2020, Dinwiddie left a game between the Nets and the [[Charlotte Hornets]] with a suspected right knee strain,{{cite web |last1=Andrews |first1=Malika |title=Nets' Spencer Dinwiddie leaves loss to Hornets with right knee strain |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30609118/nets-spencer-dinwiddie-leaves-vs-hornets-right-knee-strain |publisher=ESPN |access-date=December 28, 2020 |date=December 27, 2020}} which was later revealed to be a season-ending [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|partial ACL tear]].{{cite web |title=Spencer Dinwiddie Medical Update |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/12/28/spencer-dinwiddie-medical-update |website=Brooklyn Nets |access-date=December 28, 2020 |date=December 28, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Andrews |first1=Malika |title=Brooklyn Nets' Spencer Dinwiddie to have surgery for partially torn ACL |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30613017/brooklyn-nets-spencer-dinwiddie-surgery-partially-torn-acl |publisher=ESPN |access-date=December 28, 2020 |date=December 28, 2020}} ===Washington Wizards (2021–2022)=== On August 6, 2021, Dinwiddie was acquired by the [[Washington Wizards]] via a [[sign-and-trade deal]] involving five teams, sending [[Russell Westbrook]] to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. Dinwiddie signed a three-year deal worth $54 million and a maximum of $60 million through incentives.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/washington-acquires-six-players-five-team-trade|title=Washington acquires six players in five-team trade|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=August 6, 2021}} He made his Wizards debut on October 20, logging 13 points, four rebounds and six assists in a 98–83 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{Cite web |title=BEAL HAS 23, WIZARDS TOP RAPTORS 98–83, SPOIL TORONTO RETURN |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100006 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} On October 22, Dinwiddie scored 34 points, alongside six rebounds and nine assists, in a 135–134 overtime win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web |title=DINWIDDIE LEADS WIZARDS TO 135–134 OT WIN OVER PACERS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100019 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2022–2023)=== On February 10, 2022, Dinwiddie was traded, along with [[Dāvis Bertāns]], to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in exchange for [[Kristaps Porziņģis]] and a protected 2022 second-round pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavstradeporzingis/|publisher=National Basketball Association|title=Mavs trade Porzingis to Wizards for Dinwiddie and Bertans|access-date=February 10, 2022|date=February 10, 2022}} On March 5, Dinwiddie scored a season-high 36 points in a 114–113 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202203050DAL.html|publisher=Basketball Reference|title=Sacramento Kings at Dallas Mavericks Box Score, March 5, 2022|access-date=March 8, 2022|date=March 5, 2022}} On April 16, during Game 1 of the first round of the playoffs, he logged 22 points and eight assists in a 93–99 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{Cite magazine |title='Room For Optimism': Brunson, Dinwiddie Not Enough As Mavs Fall To Jazz in Game 1 |url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/dallas-mavs-utah-jazz-playoffs-game-one-recap-doncic-injury-dinwiddie-brunson |access-date=April 16, 2022 |magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=April 16, 2022 }} The Mavericks won the series in six games and faced the [[Phoenix Suns]] during the second round. On May 15, Dinwiddie recorded 30 points, three rebounds and two assists in a 123–90 Game 7 win over the top-seeded Suns.{{Cite web |title=DONCIC LEADS MAVS OVER SUNS 123–90 IN GAME 7 BLOWOUT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100227 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} The Mavericks advanced to the [[NBA Conference Finals|Western Conference Finals]] for the first time since [[2011 NBA playoffs|2011]] and faced the [[Golden State Warriors]]. However, the Mavericks were eliminated by the Warriors in five games, despite a 26-point, four-assist and two-block performance by Dinwiddie in a 120–110 Game 5 loss.{{Cite web |title=WARRIORS BEAT MAVERICKS 120–110 TO RETURN TO NBA FINALS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100315 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} On November 10, 2022, Dinwiddie scored 33 points, alongside four rebounds and six assists, in a 113–105 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web |title=KUZMA SCORES 36 TO LEAD WIZARDS PAST MAVERICKS 113–105 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200172 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} On January 26, 2023, he scored a season-high 36 points, alongside six rebounds and nine assists, in a 99–95 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{Cite web |title=DINWIDDIE SCORES 36, MAVS TOP SUNS 99–95 AFTER DONCIC HURT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200734 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} Two days later, Dinwiddie recorded 35 points, four rebounds and eight assists in a 108–100 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web |title=JAZZ HOLD OFF LATE RALLY, BEAT DONCIC-LESS MAVERICKS 108–100 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200750 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} ===Return to Brooklyn (2023–2024)=== On February 6, 2023, Dinwiddie was traded back to the [[Brooklyn Nets]], along with [[Dorian Finney-Smith]], an unprotected 2029 first-round pick, and second-round picks in 2027 and 2029, in exchange for [[Kyrie Irving]] and [[Markieff Morris]].{{cite web |last1=Sefko |first1=Eddie |title=Kyrie Irving coming to the Mavericks |url=https://www.mavs.com/kyrie-trade/ |website=Dallas Mavericks |date=February 6, 2023 |access-date=February 6, 2023}} On February 8, 2024, Dinwiddie was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]], in exchange for [[Dennis Schröder]] and [[Thaddeus Young]]. Following the trade, he was waived by Toronto.{{cite web|title=RAPTORS COMPLETE TRADE WITH NETS|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-complete-trade-with-nets|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}}{{cite news|first=Tim|last=Bontemps|title=Dennis Schroder traded to Nets; Raptors waive Spencer Dinwiddie|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39485030/sources-raptors-trade-dennis-schroder-nets-spencer-dinwiddie|website=ESPN.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 9, 2024}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2024)=== On February 10, 2024, Dinwiddie signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on a one-year deal worth the [[NBA salary cap#Minimum Salary Exception|league minimum]].{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Spencer Dinwiddie|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-spencer-dinwiddie-021024|website=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2024|access-date=February 10, 2024}} On March 24, 2024, Dinwiddie scored a team high 26 points, alongside two rebounds and five assists, in a 150–145 win against the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|title=Darvin Ham praises Spencer Dinwiddie after big game vs. Pacers|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/darvin-ham-praises-spencer-dinwiddie-054831172.html|website=sports.yahoo.com|date=March 24, 2024|access-date=March 26, 2024}} ===Second stint with Dallas (2024–2025)=== On August 3, 2024, Dinwiddie returned to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web |title=Mavericks announce return of 10-year veteran guard Spencer Dinwiddie|url=https://www.nba.com/news/mavericks-announce-dinwiddie-signing|date=August 4, 2024|access-date=August 4, 2024|website=nba.com}} He made 79 appearances (30 starts) for the Mavericks, averaging 11.0 points, 2.6 rebounds, and 4.4 assists. On July 13, 2025, Dinwiddie signed a one-year, $3.6 million contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web |title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Spencer Dinwiddie {{!}} Charlotte Hornets |url=https://hornets.com/news/charlotte-hornets-sign-spencer-dinwiddie |access-date=2025-07-14 |website=hornets.com |language=en}} He was waived by the Hornets on October 16.{{Cite web|title=Hornets waive veteran G Spencer Dinwiddie 3 months after signing|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46614780/sources-hornets-waiving-veteran-guard-spencer-dinwiddie|access-date=October 23, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===FC Bayern Munich (2025)=== On October 23, 2025, Dinwiddie signed a contract without a release-clause with the [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|FC Bayern Munich]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] for the remainder of the season.{{Cite web |title=Aus der NBA zu den Bayern: Spencer Dinwiddie nach München {{!}} FC Bayern Basketball |url=https://fcbayern.com/basketball/de/news/2025-26/10/verpflichtung-spencer-dinwiddie |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=fcbayern.com |language=de}} His contract was terminated on January 4, 2026 by mutual consent, due to Dinwiddie desiring to travel back to the U.S. to attend to a family member who was sick. ==National team career== In 2013, Dinwiddie was named to the USA Basketball Men's World University Games Team for the [[2013 Summer Universiade]] in [[Kazan, Russia]]. He was one of three players on Team USA to start all eight games. He averaged 7.9 points and 2.6 rebounds per game and led Team USA with 44 assists (5.5 apg) and with 12 steals (1.5 spg).{{cite web|url=https://cubuffs.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4162|title=Spencer Dinwiddie – 2013–14 Men's Basketball Roster|work=cubuffs.com|access-date=September 17, 2018}} On April 19, 2020, Dinwiddie (whose father is from Nigeria) confirmed reports that he wanted to represent the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team|Nigerian national team]].{{Cite news|url=https://m.guardian.ng/sport/behind-nigerias-bid-to-land-brooklyn-nets-spencer-dinwiddie-for-the-olympics|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=behind-nigerias-bid-to-land-brooklyn-nets-spencer-dinwiddie-for-the-olympics|date=April 22, 2020 |access-date=April 22, 2020|newspaper=[[The Guardian (Nigeria)|The Guardian]]}}{{cite web |publisher=WOAI}} ==Signature Shoe and Independent Brand== In 2018, Spencer Dinwiddie launched his own independent sneaker brand, K8IROS (pronounced "Kairos"), making him one of the few active NBA players to create and wear a self-branded signature shoe on court.https://www.slamonline.com/kicks/spencer-dinwiddie-k8iros-interview/ The brand name is derived from the Greek word for “opportune time,” reflecting Dinwiddie’s entrepreneurial mindset and desire to control his own brand identity. K8IROS sneakers were designed to be performance-ready while also offering players and fans an alternative to traditional sneaker endorsement deals. Dinwiddie wore K8IROS models throughout NBA games, using the shoes as a platform to express personal messages, support causes, and showcase custom artwork.https://www.netsdaily.com/2020/1/12/21063235/spencer-dinwiddie-explains-kairos-his-sneaker-company His move toward independent sneaker development has been noted as part of a broader trend among athletes seeking more creative and financial autonomy within the sportswear industry. In 2021, Dinwiddie partnered with Chinese sportswear brand 361°, becoming one of its leading global basketball ambassadors.https://www.boardroom.tv/spencer-dinwiddie-361-shoes-partnership/ Under this collaboration, Dinwiddie continued to develop and wear signature sneakers, with some models incorporating design DNA from his K8IROS line. The partnership allowed him to maintain creative input while expanding the brand’s reach across international markets. The collaboration with 361° represented Dinwiddie’s continued commitment to athlete empowerment and brand ownership, positioning him as both a professional basketball player and an active participant in the business of sports apparel.https://hypebeast.com/2021/12/spencer-dinwiddie-361-deal-announcement ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{commons category}} {{basketballstats}} *[https://cubuffs.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4162 Colorado Buffaloes bio] {{2014 NBA draft}} {{Portal bar|Sports}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Dinwiddie, Spencer}} [[Category:1993 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportsmen]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:21st-century Nigerian sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Los Angeles]] [[Category:Brooklyn Nets players]] [[Category:Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball players]] [[Category:Dallas Mavericks players]] [[Category:Detroit Pistons draft picks]] [[Category:Detroit Pistons players]] [[Category:FC Bayern Munich basketball players]] [[Category:Los Angeles Lakers players]] [[Category:Grand Rapids Drive players]] [[Category:Nigeria men's national basketball team players]] [[Category:People from Woodland Hills, Los Angeles]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Washington Wizards players]] [[Category:William Howard Taft Charter High School alumni]] [[Category:Windy City Bulls players]]
